# `pre-commit.yml`

## Inputs

| Name | Description | Type | Default | Required |
| :--- | :---------- | :--- | :------ | :------: |
| all_files | <pre>true (default) runs `pre-commit run --all-files`. Set false to run only the files a pull request changes, via --from-ref/--to-ref -- the direct analogue of GitLab's `--from-ref $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA --to-ref HEAD`.<br>This is not just a speed knob. A `pass_filenames: false` hook whose `files:` pattern matches a tracked file fires on EVERY --all-files run, because that file is always in the set. personal-website's generate-resume hook is one: under --all-files it would rebuild a Docker image and regenerate a resume on every pull request, rather than only when the CV changes.<br>Ignored outside a pull_request event -- there is no base to diff against, so a push or schedule falls back to --all-files.</pre> | `boolean` | `true` | no |
| extra_packages | Space-separated pip packages installed alongside pre-commit, for hooks that import them. Empty (default) installs nothing extra. | `string` | `` | no |
| fetch_depth | Checkout depth. Defaults to 0 (full history), and the default is deliberately the expensive one: a shallow clone does not make a history-reading hook FAIL, it makes it quietly WRONG. `git log -1 --format=%ad -- <file>` on a truncated clone returns the shallow boundary commit's date instead of the file's real last-touch date -- a plausible wrong answer, not an empty one. Measured in the docs repo at depth 20: architecture/custom-keys.md reported 2026-07-22 against a true 2026-07-14, and redis-sentinel-ha.md reported 2026-07-22 against a true 2026-07-20. Set 1 only when you have checked that no hook reads git history, and expect to save seconds, not minutes. | `number` | `0` | no |
| python_version | Python used to run pre-commit itself, not the hooks | `string` | `3.13` | no |
| runner_labels | Runner labels as JSON array (e.g., ["self-hosted", "oke"]) | `string` | `["ubuntu-24.04"]` | no |
